resource.name: aws_kinesis_stream
resource.description: Provides a Kinesis Stream resource. Amazon Kinesis is a managed service that scales elastically for real-time processing of streaming big data. For more details, see the Amazon Kinesis Documentation.
resource.llm_summary: "Manages the creation and configuration of an Amazon Kinesis Stream for real-time ingestion and processing of streaming data at scale. Common use cases include building data pipelines, enabling real-time analytics, and integrating with AWS services like Lambda, S3, and DynamoDB for event-driven architectures. Supports configurations for shard capacity, retention periods, encryption, and enhanced monitoring to optimize performance and security for high-throughput data streams."

examples.title: Basic Usage
examples.llm_summary: This example demonstrates how to configure an AWS Kinesis stream with a provisioned stream mode, specifying shard count, retention period, and shard-level metrics for monitoring. It also illustrates the use of tags for resource categorization and the `stream_mode_details` block for advanced stream mode settings.

arguments.name: arn
arguments.llm_summary: The `arn` argument in the `aws_kinesis_stream` resource represents the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Kinesis stream, which uniquely identifies the stream within AWS. While not required to configure the resource, it is typically used for referencing the stream in other resources, policies, or integrations, enabling users to link the stream to IAM roles, permissions, or dependent services.

arguments.name: encryption_type
arguments.description: (Optional) The encryption type to use. The only acceptable values are `NONE` or `KMS`. The default value is `NONE`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `encryption_type` argument for the `aws_kinesis_stream` resource allows users to specify the encryption mechanism for securing data within the stream, with options of `NONE` for no encryption or `KMS` for server-side encryption using AWS Key Management Service. Configuring this argument helps users meet security and compliance requirements by enabling or disabling encryption for data at rest in the Kinesis stream.

arguments.name: enforce_consumer_deletion
arguments.description: (Optional) A boolean that indicates all registered consumers should be deregistered from the stream so that the stream can be destroyed without error. The default value is `false`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `enforce_consumer_deletion` argument in the `aws_kinesis_stream` resource controls whether all registered consumers are automatically deregistered from the stream during its destruction, ensuring the stream can be deleted without errors caused by lingering consumer dependencies. This argument is typically used to simplify lifecycle management by preventing deletion failures in scenarios where consumer cleanup is required.

arguments.name: id
arguments.llm_summary: The `id` argument for the `aws_kinesis_stream` resource represents the unique identifier of the Kinesis stream, typically auto-generated by AWS upon creation. While optional, specifying this argument allows users to reference the stream's ID explicitly for integration with other resources or workflows, enabling precise identification and interaction within their cloud infrastructure.

arguments.name: kms_key_id
arguments.description: (Optional) The GUID for the customer-managed KMS key to use for encryption. You can also use a Kinesis-owned master key by specifying the alias `alias/aws/kinesis`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `kms_key_id` argument for the `aws_kinesis_stream` resource allows users to specify the customer-managed KMS key or the Kinesis-owned master key (`alias/aws/kinesis`) for encrypting data within the stream. Configuring this argument enables enhanced security by defining the encryption mechanism for data at rest, aligning with compliance requirements or organizational security policies.

arguments.name: name
arguments.description: (Required) A name to identify the stream. This is unique to the AWS account and region the Stream is created in.
arguments.llm_summary: The `name` argument for the `aws_kinesis_stream` resource specifies a unique identifier for the stream within the AWS account and region, enabling users to define a distinct and recognizable name for organizing and referencing the stream in their infrastructure. Setting this argument is essential for creating and managing the stream, as it serves as a key property for resource identification and integration with other AWS services.

arguments.name: retention_period
arguments.description: (Optional) Length of time data records are accessible after they are added to the stream. The maximum value of a stream's retention period is 8760 hours. Minimum value is 24. Default is 24.
arguments.llm_summary: The `retention_period` argument for the `aws_kinesis_stream` resource allows users to define the duration, in hours, that data records remain accessible in the stream after ingestion. By configuring this argument, users can control the stream's data retention lifecycle to meet specific use cases, such as compliance, analytics, or long-term data availability, with a range between 24 and 8760 hours (defaulting to 24 hours).

arguments.name: shard_count
arguments.description: – (Optional) The number of shards that the stream will use. If the `stream_mode` is `PROVISIONED`, this field is required. Amazon has guidelines for specifying the Stream size that should be referenced when creating a Kinesis stream. See Amazon Kinesis Streams for more.
arguments.llm_summary: The `shard_count` argument in the `aws_kinesis_stream` resource specifies the number of shards allocated to the stream, directly controlling its capacity to handle data throughput and parallelism. This is essential for provisioning streams in `PROVISIONED` mode, enabling users to scale data ingestion and processing based on workload requirements while adhering to AWS guidelines for stream sizing.

arguments.name: shard_level_metrics
arguments.description: (Optional) A list of shard-level CloudWatch metrics which can be enabled for the stream. See Monitoring with CloudWatch for more. Note that the value ALL should not be used; instead you should provide an explicit list of metrics you wish to enable.
arguments.llm_summary: The `shard_level_metrics` argument for the `aws_kinesis_stream` resource allows users to specify a set of shard-level CloudWatch metrics to monitor the performance and activity of individual shards within the stream. By enabling specific metrics, users can gain deeper insights into shard-level operations, such as incoming and outgoing data rates, enhancing observability and facilitating troubleshooting or optimization of the stream's behavior.

arguments.name: tags
arguments.description: (Optional) A map of tags to assign to the resource. If configured with a provider `default_tags` configuration block present, tags with matching keys will overwrite those defined at the provider-level.
arguments.llm_summary: The `tags` argument for the `aws_kinesis_stream` resource allows users to assign key-value metadata to the stream, enabling organization, categorization, and identification of resources for purposes such as cost allocation, environment labeling, or compliance tracking. When set, it overrides provider-level default tags with matching keys, ensuring granular control over resource tagging.

arguments.name: tags_all
arguments.llm_summary: The `tags_all` argument for the `aws_kinesis_stream` resource allows users to define a comprehensive set of key-value tags inherited from both provider-level and resource-specific configurations. This enables streamlined resource organization, cost allocation, and metadata management by consolidating all tags applied to the Kinesis stream, supporting common goals like environment labeling, compliance tracking, and operational categorization.

blocks.name: stream_mode_details
blocks.description: (Optional) Indicates the capacity mode of the data stream. Detailed below.

arguments.name: stream_mode
arguments.llm_summary: The `stream_mode` argument in the `stream_mode_details` block of the `aws_kinesis_stream` resource specifies the operational mode of the Kinesis stream, allowing users to define whether the stream operates in **"ON_DEMAND"** or **"PROVISIONED"** mode. This configuration impacts scalability and cost management, enabling users to optimize the stream for dynamic workloads (on-demand) or predictable traffic patterns (provisioned) based on their application's throughput requirements.

blocks.llm_summary: The `stream_mode_details` block in the `aws_kinesis_stream` resource configures the capacity mode of the Kinesis data stream, enabling users to choose between on-demand or provisioned throughput modes. This block allows for precise control over stream scaling and cost optimization, helping users tailor the stream's performance to their workload requirements.

blocks.name: timeouts

arguments.name: create
arguments.llm_summary: The `create` argument within the `timeouts` block of the `aws_kinesis_stream` resource allows users to specify the maximum duration (as a string, e.g., "10m") Terraform will wait for the Kinesis stream to be successfully created. Configuring this timeout helps manage deployment workflows by preventing indefinite waits or premature failures during stream creation, aligning with user-defined operational expectations.

arguments.name: delete
arguments.llm_summary: The `delete` argument within the `timeouts` block for the `aws_kinesis_stream` resource allows users to specify the maximum duration (as a string, e.g., "5m" for 5 minutes) Terraform will wait for the deletion of a Kinesis stream to complete. Configuring this timeout ensures predictable resource lifecycle management, particularly in scenarios where stream deletion may take longer due to AWS processing delays or dependencies.

arguments.name: update
arguments.llm_summary: The `update` argument within the `timeouts` block for the `aws_kinesis_stream` resource allows users to specify the maximum duration (as a string) Terraform will wait for updates to the Kinesis stream to complete. By configuring this timeout, users can control the behavior of long-running update operations, ensuring smoother resource management and avoiding potential timeout errors during stream modifications.

blocks.llm_summary: The `timeouts` configuration block in the `aws_kinesis_stream` resource allows users to define custom timeout durations for specific operations, such as creating, updating, or deleting a Kinesis stream. By configuring this block, users gain precise control over operation time limits, ensuring smoother management of stream lifecycle actions in environments with varying performance or resource constraints.
